note.en: What you see: During the pulse check the subxiphoid window opens onto the beating or still heart. Organised cardiac motion with a pulse means return of circulation, while organised motion without a pulse is pulseless electrical activity. A still heart with no motion through the pause is asystole. Clotted blood inside a chamber can mimic wall motion, so motion must be judged across the full pause with the gain set fairly.

steps.en: What you see: During the pulse check the subxiphoid window opens onto the beating or still heart. Organised cardiac motion with a pulse means return of circulation, while organised motion without a pulse is pulseless electrical activity. A still heart with no motion through the pause is asystole. Clotted blood inside a chamber can mimic wall motion, so motion must be judged across the full pause with the gain set fairly.
Landmarks to confirm: Heart with four chambers where visible, pericardium, liver as the window, femoral or carotid pulse correlation by the bedside team.

Common mistakes and correction: Letting the scan prolong the pause beyond the limit: the probe must lift when time is called. Calling clot motion true wall motion: confirm organised contraction of the walls, not drifting echoes. Starting the scan only when compressions stop: pre position during compressions so the pause holds only recording.

Normal values with units: The pause limit is 10 seconds or less from stop to restart of compressions. Reversible causes to seek on the scan are tamponade fluid, tension pneumothorax signs and profound empty chambers. No single scan finding alone decides stopping resuscitation.

Pitfalls: The scan must never delay compressions, drugs or defibrillation, so the team leader owns the clock. A poor window in a moving trolley case is common, so record the limitation instead of guessing. Share the clip with the team rather than whispering the finding to one member.

todo.en: How to get it step by step: Keep the probe ready on the belly during compressions without interrupting them. At the pause, place it subxiphoid flat and aimed at the left shoulder. Record a short clip of the heart through the pause. Call out what is seen in plain words: beating with pulse, motion without pulse, or still. Resume compressions the moment the pause limit is reached, then report the clip to the team leader.

remember.en: Hold every pause to 10 seconds or less

q.en: What is the pause limit for the pulse check echo?

o.en: No limit when the image is unclear

why.en: Compressions must restart within 10 seconds, so the scan fits inside that pause.

q.en: What is pulseless electrical activity on the scan?

why.en: Organised wall motion without a palpable pulse defines pulseless electrical activity.

q.en: How is the pause kept within the limit?

o.en: Pre position during compressions and lift when time is called
Start searching only after compressions stop
Delay drugs until the clip is reviewed

why.en: Pre positioning means the pause holds only recording, and lifting on time protects compressions.
